# `device` records

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask docs-gen` from schemas/0.1/device.schema.json. Do not edit: change the source and regenerate. -->

Everything with one tag; the single owner of parts (ADR-0006, doc 03 §7, rank 31). The printed tag is
derived from `tag`, the numbering scheme and the main representation; it is stored nowhere.

Aspects follow the known members, flattened in the order of doc 05 §3.1: `strip`, `terminal`, `cable`,
`assembly`, `plc_station`, `plc_module`, then `bus_node` and `valve_terminal`. Typed: `strip`, `terminal`,
`cable`, `assembly` (cycle 15, D-41), `plc_station` and `plc_module`; `bus_node` and `valve_terminal` arrive
with their work packages and are kept in `extra` until then, which places them after the typed aspects.
`user_props` has no field-level definition yet and is kept in `extra` too.

Deserialisation takes the aspects out of the object first and reads each at its own path, because
serde reads flattened fields from a buffer that loses the paths of errors inside them.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | `device` |
| File | `devices/<xx>.jsonl` |
| Rank | 31 |
| Status | implemented |
| Record version | 1 |
| Schema | [`device.schema.json`](https://github.com/Ironkode787/ElektraWatt/blob/main/schemas/0.1/device.schema.json) |

## Types

### Assembly

The `Assembly` aspect (doc 03 §7, FR-DEV-020, FR-DEV-022, D-36, D-41): the configurator order codes of a
configured product whose children are the devices with this device as `parent` (ordered by `position`).

In the assembly BOM (`bom_rows(Assembly)`, FR-REP-005) every config that names a `part` prints one row
and replaces the own part lines of the devices it `covers`, unless `bom_basis` is `components`.

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bom_basis` | [`BomBasis`](#bombasis) | no |  | What the assembly BOM lists for this assembly; default the configured products. |
| `configs` | array of [`AssemblyConfig`](#assemblyconfig) | no |  | The order codes, in order (order code 1 first). |

### AssemblyConfig

One configurator order code of an assembly (doc 03 §7).

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `covers` | array of [`Uuid`](#uuid) (items unique) | no |  | The devices whose own part lines this order code replaces in the assembly BOM: the assembly device itself or its descendants, each named explicitly (not transitive). |
| `label` | [`MlText`](#mltext) | no |  | The label ("Order Code 1"); empty when unset. |
| `order_code` | [`Ident`](#ident) | yes |  | The order code, stored verbatim (doc 10 §2.3). |
| `part` | [`PartRef`](#partref) or `null` | no |  | The configured part copy (kind `configured`, FR-PRT-006) that the assembly BOM prints for it. |

### BomBasis

What the assembly BOM lists for an assembly (doc 03 §7).

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `"assembly"` | One row per configured product, replacing the covered parts (the default). |
| `"components"` | The component parts, as in the component BOM. |

### Ident

An identifier: non-empty, one line (no control character U+0000 to U+001F or U+007F to U+009F), without leading or trailing white space (the Unicode White_Space set); interior spaces are allowed (doc 05 §3.2). JSON Schema cannot express Unicode Normalization Form C; the reader rejects non-NFC text.

Type: string (at least 1 character(s))

Pattern: `^[^\u0000-\u0020\u007F-\u00A0\u1680\u2000-\u200A\u2028\u2029\u202F\u205F\u3000](?:[^\u0000-\u001F\u007F-\u009F]*[^\u0000-\u0020\u007F-\u00A0\u1680\u2000-\u200A\u2028\u2029\u202F\u205F\u3000])?$`

### LengthSource

The source of a cable length (FR-CBL-009). The committed sources `Estimated` and `Routed` (1.0) are
additive variants of a later format.

One of the following forms:

1. **Form 1**: No length yet (the default); blocks release.

   Shape: `"missing"`

2. **Form 2**: Entered by hand.

   Shape: object { `manual`: [`Nm`](#nm) }

   | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `manual` | [`Nm`](#nm) | yes |  | A length in nanometres (doc 05 §3.2). Written without fraction or exponent; JSON Schema cannot tell 5 from 5.0, the reader rejects the latter. |

3. **Form 3**: From the cable part (pre-assembled length).

   Shape: `"from_part"`

### MlText

Multilingual text: a neutral string, or an object keyed by canonical BCP 47 tags with non-empty string values (doc 05 §3.2). JSON Schema cannot express that all text is NFC or that the keys are in ascending byte order; the reader rejects both.

One of the following forms:

1. **Form 1**

   Shape: string

2. **Form 2**

   Shape: map of string (at least 1 character(s)) (at least 1 propert(ies))

### Nm

A length in nanometres (doc 05 §3.2). Written without fraction or exponent; JSON Schema cannot tell 5 from 5.0, the reader rejects the latter.

Type: integer (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991)

### PartUse

A part use on a device (ADR-0006): the part and its quantity in the part's order unit.

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `part` | [`PartRef`](#partref) | yes |  | The part. |
| `qty` | [`Dec3`](#dec3) | yes |  | The quantity in the part's order unit (pieces, metres, sets). |

### Dec3

A canonical decimal string: at most three fraction digits, no trailing fraction zeros, no leading zeros, no plus sign, no "-0", no exponent, no white space, no unit (doc 05 §3.2). The pattern bounds the integer part to 16 digits; the exact i64 range of the thousandths (about 9.2 x 10^15) is checked by the reader.

Type: string (at most 21 character(s))

Pattern: `^(?:0|-?[1-9][0-9]{0,15}(?:\.[0-9]{0,2}[1-9])?|-?0\.[0-9]{0,2}[1-9])$`

| `slot` | [`SlotPath`](#slotpath) | no |  | The slot; default positional (the rank among the station's modules by `Device.position`). |
| `start` | [`IoStarts`](#iostarts) | no |  | The start address per direction; default `auto` for both. |

### AddrSpec

An address specification (doc 10 §2.5): derived, deliberate, excluded or open.

One of the following forms:

1. **Form 1**: Module start plus the address-map offset (the default).

   Shape: `"auto"`

2. **Form 2**: A deliberate value; every deviation from the derived value is reported (EW-PLC-012).

   Shape: object { `manual`: [`PlcAddress`](#plcaddress) }

   | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `manual` | [`PlcAddress`](#plcaddress) | yes |  | A canonical PLC address (doc 10 §2.5), rendered by the configuration project's profile. |

3. **Form 3**: Not addressed ("do not include in addressing").

   Shape: `"excluded"`

4. **Form 4**: A typed open item; prints "TBD" and blocks release (EW-PLC-015).

   Shape: `"tbd"`

### StructureAssignment

Which structure node a page, device or structure box belongs to, one slot per aspect (doc 03 §5).
Members follow the canonical aspect order of `ew_rds::Aspect`; the product aspect is the device tree and
has no slot.

```
use ew_schema::StructureAssignment;

let s: StructureAssignment = serde_json::from_str(
    r#"{"function":"7d2c95e0-1f4a-5b38-a6e7-0c93b5d1f284","location":"none"}"#,
).unwrap();
assert!(s.installation_site.is_none()); // absent: inherit
```

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `document_kind` | [`Slot`](#slot) or `null` | no |  | `&` (pages only). |
| `function` | [`Slot`](#slot) or `null` | no |  | `=` |
| `functional_assignment` | [`Slot`](#slot) or `null` | no |  | `==` |
| `installation_site` | [`Slot`](#slot) or `null` | no |  | `++` |
| `location` | [`Slot`](#slot) or `null` | no |  | `+` |
| `type` | [`Slot`](#slot) or `null` | no |  | `%` |
| `user_defined` | [`Slot`](#slot) or `null` | no |  | `#` |

### Slot

2. **Form 2**

### TechValue

One technical value (doc 05 §3.2 `TechValue`): `{"key", "value"}` whose value is a `Quantity` or an
`Ident`, told apart by JSON type.

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | [`Ident`](#ident) | yes |  | The property key, such as `i_out` or `curve`. |
| `value` | [`TechVal`](#techval) | yes |  | The value. |

### TechVal

The value of a `TechValue`, told apart by JSON type: an object is a `Quantity`, a string an
`Ident`. Any other JSON type is kept as `TechVal::Unknown`; an object that is not a quantity or a
string that is not an identifier is a malformed variant (`quantity`, `ident`).

One of the following forms:

1. **Form 1**: A quantity such as 20 A.

   Shape: [`Quantity`](#quantity)

2. **Form 2**: An identifier such as the tripping curve `C`.

   Shape: [`Ident`](#ident)

### Quantity

A decimal value with its unit (doc 03 §3.2): `{"value": Dec3, "unit": Unit}`. Rendering ("0.75 mm²",
decimal comma in nl and de) is a query, never stored text (D-18).

```
use ew_schema::{Quantity, Unit};

let q: Quantity = serde_json::from_str(r#"{"value":"20","unit":"A"}"#).unwrap();
assert_eq!(q.unit, Unit::A);
assert_eq!(serde_json::to_string(&q).unwrap(), r#"{"value":"20","unit":"A"}"#);
```

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `unit` | [`Unit`](#unit) | yes |  | Its unit. |
| `value` | [`Dec3`](#dec3) | yes |  | The number. |

### Uuid

A lower-case hyphenated UUID (doc 05 §3.2).

Type: string (at least 36 character(s), at most 36 character(s))

Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$`
